correction.cliopatria: Sovereign Principality of the United Netherlands
correction.text: the liberated Northern Netherlands in November-December 1813: the 1814 shape applied back; the page names no boundary

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's row starts in 1814 but the Triumvirate 'formally took control over the liberated country on 20 November' 1813 and William was proclaimed Sovereign Prince on 2 December 1813. The page does not say which fortresses or districts were still French in 1813, so the 1814 shape is extended back with that caveat. Cliopatria's First French Empire shape for 1813 still covers Amsterdam, so the two overlap in this year.

35,750 km2, the Northern Netherlands only. The page gives no area (only 2,233,000 inhabitants in 1815). Belgium is not in the shape; the page puts it under Allied military government in February 1814 and awards it to the Dutch state in May-August 1814 (ledger). The United Kingdom of the Netherlands page gives 68,095 km2 for the kingdom (no year), against 35,750 km2 here plus Belgium, so the shape is of the right order.

region.cliopatria: Sovereign Principality of the United Netherlands
region.text: 'the liberated country': the Northern Netherlands freed from France by Prussian and Russian troops in 1813

ledger.note: 20 November 1813: the Triumvirate 'formally took control over the liberated country' and declares the principality; William Frederick lands at Scheveningen on 30 November and is proclaimed Sovereign Prince on 2 December 1813, with Amsterdam as capital.

region.text: Belgium on the left bank of the Meuse (Treaty of Paris, 30 May 1814) and 'the former Austrian Netherlands' (Eight Articles of London, 21 June 1814)

ledger.note: 1 August 1814: William becomes Governor-General of Belgium. The page: Belgium, 'conquered by France in 1794 and annexed in 1795', was placed under Allied military government in February 1814; the Treaty of Paris (30 May 1814) apportioned the left bank of the Meuse to the future Netherlands 'with the right bank's fate left open'; the Eight Articles of London (21 June 1814) 'awarded him the former Austrian Netherlands'. Formal union follows in March 1815; the extent east of the Meuse is not settled on the page.

union.cliopatria: Sovereign Principality of the United Netherlands

region.text: the principality and the Belgian lands, merged into the kingdom

ledger.note: 16 March 1815: William is proclaimed King William I of the United Kingdom of the Netherlands, which ends the principality (the United Kingdom page: he 'declare[d] himself king on 16 March 1815'; Brussels as the place is on the principality page only).

wars.name: War of the Sixth Coalition

zones.text: the Northern Netherlands, liberated from France in 1813
Belgium, under Allied military government from February 1814

wars.outcome: The French lost the Netherlands to Prussian and Russian troops in 1813 and Belgium to Allied military government in February 1814; the Treaty of Paris (30 May 1814) apportioned the left bank of the Meuse to the future Netherlands.
wars.note: Only the Dutch episode is read, from the principality's page; the war's own article was not opened (page budget). The page gives no dates for the campaigns in the Netherlands, so no contest events are recorded.

certainty.note: Neither page gives a boundary of the Northern Netherlands in 1813-1814; the Treaty of Paris left the Belgian right bank of the Meuse open.

sources.title: United Kingdom of the Netherlands
sources.note: 16 March 1815 kingship, infobox area 68,095 km2 (no year), Luxembourg, Governor-General in August 1814; used for the area check.

notes: Cliopatria draws only 1814 (35,750 km2: the Northern Netherlands); the page dates the principality from 20 November 1813 to 16 March 1815, hence a new 1813 keyframe and a dissolve in 1815, a year the Cliopatria 'netherlands' row already covers (with Belgium), so the renderer should let that row take 1815. Belgium is not in the 1814 shape; it enters by the August 1814 gain. The Anglo-Dutch Treaty (13 August 1814, colonies) is only a name in the infobox and the Luxembourg grand duchy is undated on the pages opened, so neither is recorded. Cliopatria's First French Empire shape covers Brussels, Antwerp and Amsterdam in 1813 and none in 1814. Not read (budget): Eight Articles of London, Treaty of Paris (1814), War of the Sixth Coalition.
